$comment: D-C-DECODEFLOAT-TREATS-UNDERFLOW-AS-FATAL: a `double` literal that UNDERFLOWS compiles and carries the reference bit pattern. Every literal in main.c was a HARD COMPILE ERROR before this fix — `error[H_UnsupportedLoweringForKind]: literal '1e-320' is out of range / undecodable`, ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 — because `decodeFloat` read `strtod`'s ERANGE as a single verdict. C23 7.24.1.5 gives that one errno to two OPPOSITE outcomes and separates them by the RETURNED VALUE: an OVERFLOW returns ±HUGE_VAL, an UNDERFLOW returns a magnitude no greater than the smallest normal. Underflow to a subnormal is an ordinary representable binary64 value, so the refusal refused correct programs. ★ THE FILE READS BYTES, NOT ONLY 'it compiles': a compile-only pin cannot tell a correct decode from one that silently lost the value, which is the exact failure mode a fix in this direction risks. Every expected pattern was ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 from the static initializer a reference compiler ACTUALLY EMITTED, all four agreeing byte-for-byte — gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (WSL, probed separately), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, and MSVC cl.exe 19.51.36252, which accepts every one silently with no warning even at /W4. ★★ THE FLUSH-TO-ZERO BOUNDARY IS PINNED ON PURPOSE, because it is where the over-correction and the under-correction both land: `2e-324` and `1e-330` underflow all the way to +0.0 and are STILL accepted by all four references, so neither 'refuse every underflow' nor 'refuse anything reaching zero' is the reference behaviour. The smallest NORMAL is pinned as the control — it sets no ERANGE, always compiled, and must not move. Order relations are checked alongside the bytes so a decode that collapsed every underflow to zero could not pass by matching a pattern regenerated from DSS itself. ⓘ No axis probe, unlike the `long double` sibling: `double` is binary64 on every target DSS ships, so one expected pattern is right on all four legs. exit = 42; any other code names the failing check.
